project: Hotel room booking: rooms, guests, bookings, payment and notification ports.
canonicalSource: Cockburn, A. (2005). Hexagonal architecture (Ports and Adapters). alistair.cockburn.us/hexagonal-architecture. Allowed-dependency graph from presets/hexagonal.yaml and Docs/v1.3-hexagonal-notes.md.
styleDefinition: The application (domain + application layers) is the inside of the hexagon; it talks to the outside only through ports it owns (driving ports in application/ports/in, driven ports in application/ports/out).

Allowed dependencies (preset): application -> domain; adapters-inbound -> application, domain; adapters-outbound -> application, domain; config -> every layer. Everything else across layers is a violation.
The domain depends on nothing outside itself and on no framework.
Driven (outbound) adapters implement a port declared inside the hexagon; driving (inbound) adapters call driving ports.
Use cases receive driven ports (interfaces), never adapter classes.
Inbound and outbound adapters never import each other; only the composition root (config) knows both.
